Plan sample size from a pilot variance prior and a planned effect distribution

Source: R/tidyMS_power_fdr.R
power_fdr_prior_n.Rd

Fit a variance prior to per-feature pilot variances and residual degrees of freedom, then integrate ordinary two-sided t-test power over that prior and the user's planned distribution of non-null effects.

Usage

power_fdr_prior_n(
  var,
  df,
  delta_mean,
  delta_se = 0,
  fdr = 0.05,
  power = 0.8,
  pi0 = 0.95,
  max_n = 100
)

Arguments

var

real numeric vector of unweighted, unmoderated within-group variance estimates on the response scale (usually log2 intensity). Non-finite values are excluded; finite negative variances are errors.

df

real numeric vector of residual degrees of freedom, either length one (shared by all features) or length(var). Non-finite and non-positive values are excluded together with their variance estimate.

delta_mean

one finite mean difference among non-null features, on the same scale as the pilot response; negative or zero means are allowed.

delta_se

one finite, non-negative standard deviation of the true differences among non-null features. This is not the standard error of an estimated mean effect. Zero specifies one fixed planned effect.

fdr

one target false discovery rate, strictly between zero and one.

power

one target average power among non-null features, strictly between zero and one.

pi0

one assumed proportion of truly null features, strictly between zero and one; it is not estimated from the pilot.

max_n

one whole number of at least two: the largest sample count per group to consider.

Value

A list containing N (first integer sample count per group reaching the target, or NA_integer_), power_achieved (at N, or at max_n when the target is not reached), power_curve (a tibble of n and power for 2 through max_n), sig_level, var_prior, df_prior, n_features_used, and the original inputs var, df, delta_mean, delta_se, fdr, power, pi0, max_n.

Details

At least three usable features, including two positive variances, are needed to estimate the prior with limma::squeezeVar(var, df, robust = FALSE). Zero variances are retained; any limma warnings about unreliable or offset variances remain visible. If the estimated prior parameters are \(s_0^2\) and \(d_0\), true variances follow an inverse-gamma distribution with shape \(d_0/2\) and scale \(d_0 s_0^2/2\). True non-null differences independently follow Normal(delta_mean, delta_se) (mean and standard deviation).

Deterministic midpoint quadrature uses gamma-precision and normal-effect quantiles: 256 variance nodes (1024 when prior df is below four) and 512 effect nodes. Infinite prior df gives the single variance var_prior; zero delta_se gives the single effect delta_mean.

The power curve uses the fixed threshold from fdr_sig_level() at the requested target power. The chosen sample size achieves the FDR planning bound under those assumptions; points below the target power need not. Prospective tests use 2 * n - 2 degrees of freedom, not moderated df. A moderated test gains prior degrees of freedom, so this ordinary t-test sample size is conservative relative to that test under the same model. This function estimates the variance distribution, not effects or pi0.

References

Jung SH (2005). Sample size for FDR-control in microarray data analysis. Bioinformatics 21:3097–3104. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bti456 . Liu P, Hwang JTG (2007). Quick calculation for sample size while controlling false discovery rate with application to microarray analysis. Bioinformatics 23:739–746. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btl664 .

Examples

variances <- 0.01 * stats::qf((seq_len(200) - 0.5) / 200, df1 = 8, df2 = 10)
planned <- power_fdr_prior_n(variances, df = 8, delta_mean = 0.15, delta_se = 0.02)
planned[c("N", "power_achieved", "var_prior", "df_prior", "n_features_used")]
#> $N
#> [1] 21
#> 
#> $power_achieved
#> [1] 0.8177378
#> 
#> $var_prior
#> [1] 0.01000914
#> 
#> $df_prior
#> [1] 10.07975
#> 
#> $n_features_used
#> [1] 200
#>
